- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral; model reacts too slowly to downward pressure.
- Model consistently overpredicts mid-to-late horizon (days 15–30) when sentiment is positive, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment turns positive mid-period, model fails to adjust downward in the following 5–7 days; introduce a 3–5 day lag correction for sentiment-driven reversals.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after 10–15 days of upward momentum; apply a 10% downward adjustment if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope by 15–20% for next 7 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
